title: tool-contract-canonicalizer-and-idempotent-invoke-protocol-for-openai-compat
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers reported inconsistent tool/schema mapping between Redwood's streaming API and OpenAI-style function/tool calling, causing duplicate tool invocations when clients retried partial streams. This PR introduces a canonical 'tool contract' layer that normalizes incoming tool definitions, a streaming fragment reconciliation step that reassembles partial tool payloads deterministically, and an idempotent-invoke protocol to prevent duplicate side-effecting calls. Changes are implemented in a backward-compatible way with a feature flag (openai_tool_contract_v1) that defaults on for new API keys and can be toggled per-tenant. Implementation summary: 1) introduced pkg/openai/compat/contract_canonicalizer.go to produce a deterministic canonical representation for tool schemas (sorts args, normalizes types, injects stable ids where missing); 2) added streaming/fragment_reassembly.go to buffer and reassemble tool-invoke fragments with sequence and checksum validation; 3) implemented an invoke-middleware in server/handlers/invoke_middleware.go that attaches an idempotency token derived from canonical tool contract + prompt KV hash and enforces at-least-once-to-once semantics against the invoke-store; 4) extended telemetry endpoints to emit tool_contract_id and fragment_reassembly latency metrics; 5) test harness and compatibility shims for OpenAI-compat adapter in pkg/adapters/openai_adapter.go; 6) docs and migration guide under docs/openai_tool_contract.md. Compatibility notes: when feature flag is off, runtime falls back to previous behavior; the middleware is enabled only for OpenAI-compat routes and for routes with schema-based tool calls. Testing: extensive unit tests for canonicalizer and fragment reassembly, integration tests that run streaming tool calls with deliberate mid-stream disconnects and retries, and a small perf benchmark to assert <5% median latency regression. Rollout plan: gated rollout to 10% of Hosted API traffic for one week, then 50% with extra alerting, followed by full ramp if no regressions. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] docs updated [x] feature flag added [x] canary rollout plan documented. Related: ENG-1342 (contract normalization), SUP-321 (customer incident reproduced).

review_conversation: Mateo Ruiz (reviewer): Can we avoid adding stable ids for nested anonymous objects? Concern about inflating contracts. Response (Asha): We only inject stable ids for top-level unnamed tool args when proto/type information is missing; added an opt-out rule in canonicalizer. Mateo: OK after change.
Jing Wei (reviewer): Add unit tests that include complex type unions and ordering randomness. Response (Asha): Added shuffled-schema test vectors and CI runs pass.

Sunita Rao (reviewer): How will this interact with Dedicated/API routing fallback? Response (Asha): Middleware is applied post-routing; for Dedicated traffic the same idempotency store config is used and we added config knobs to prefer local store. Sunita: LGTM.
Ravi Menon (author of one commit): Left small nit about logging. Asha: Addressed by removing verbose prints and making debug logs gated by feature flag.
Approvals: Mateo Ruiz approved, Jing Wei approved, Sunita Rao approved.
release_notes: Adds an OpenAI-compat tool contract canonicalizer and idempotent invoke middleware. Introduces feature flag openai_tool_contract_v1. Improves streaming stability for tool/function calls and prevents duplicate side-effecting invocations on client retries. Backward compatible when flag is off. Migration guide in docs/openai_tool_contract.md.
notes: Canary rollout started 2026-03-02 at 03:00 UTC to 10% of hosted traffic. Observability dashboards updated. Ops runbook entry created for triggering rollback on increased 5xx or duplicate-invoke telemetry.
